text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"---"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT :- 1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 24-32 HRC. 2) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The title block heat treatment field is '---' while note N2 specifies toughening to 24-32 HRC, and neither states the manufacturing stage at which the treatment applies. This ambiguity can cause the part to be machined after hardening or hardened at the wrong time, leading to scrap or incorrect properties. The designer should fill in the heat treatment field consistently with N2 and specify when the treatment occurs (e.g., before final machining).","recommended_correction":"Update the heat treatment field to match N2 and add the process stage (e.g., 'before finish machining') to the note."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D1","page":1,"quote":"-0.007"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D2","page":1,"quote":"-0.020"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"NOTE : # MATERIAL : EN-91 # FINISH : E.N.P. # MACHINING :"}],"comment":"Note N3 calls for E.N.P. (electroless nickel plating), but dimensions D1 and D2 have tolerance bands of 0.007 mm and 0.020 mm respectively, which are well under 0.1 mm, with no allowance made for the plating thickness. The added plating will push these tight features out of tolerance, preventing proper assembly. The designer must either open the pre-plate tolerances to absorb the coating thickness or add a note specifying post-plating rework.","recommended_correction":"Adjust the pre-plate limits on D1 and D2 to account for E.N.P. thickness, or add a note requiring post-plating sizing."}]}
